rubric_items.reason: Uses only existing modules and layers: SQL in PatientRepo, rules in PatientService, the existing route and client. There is no new endpoint, table or infrastructure, and the existing patient_id index is reused.

Every story and AC is mapped. S-1 is served by CO-1..CO-5 and EP-1, with AC5 handled by the patient_id scope. S-2 is served by the status filter, including AC4. S-3 is served because CO-5 only inserts a block and CO-8 and the medical history are untouched.

EP-1 gives visitSummary and both subfields with name, type, nullability, format and example. EP-2 and EP-3 reference the same shape and give the new-patient value of 0 and 0. CO-3 states the exact TS type.
Files and types are proven by sym facts and code lines, and the field shape is decided by A-03. However, the 100-row cap (C8) is cited second-hand through an impact claim instead of the product line.

Explains why the counts are computed on the server (the cap), why POST and PATCH also carry the field (shared get), why it counts by status rather than date, why no migration is needed (index) and the label-wording default.
Clear and consistent. The frontmatter and body match, and the component-to-story mapping is explicit.

findings.text: C8, the 100-row cap that justifies server-side counting, cites another artifact's claim (impact.md#claim:C6) rather than the product code line that defines the cap.
